question.text: Saffron Capital Pvt. Ltd., a family-owned body corporate, seeks Accredited Investor certification to participate in an LVF. Its last audited accounts show: Paid-up capital INR 20 crore, Free Reserves INR 40 crore, Accumulated Losses INR 5 crore, Unwritten-off Deferred Expenditure INR 3 crore. Does it qualify?

answer.text: Yes — net worth of INR 60 crore meets the INR 50 crore body-corporate threshold
Yes — capital plus reserves alone is INR 60 crore, comfortably above INR 50 crore
No — computed net worth is INR 52 crore, but body-corporate AI threshold is INR 100 crore
Yes — computed net worth = (20 + 40) – (5 + 3) = INR 52 crore, which exceeds the INR 50 crore body-corporate AI threshold

explanation.text: The Logic: Body-corporate AI threshold is net worth ≥ INR 50 crore. Net Worth for a body corporate = (Capital + Free Reserves) – (Accumulated Losses + Deferred Expenditure not written off) = (20 + 40) – (5 + 3) = INR 52 crore. This clears the INR 50 crore minimum. The Trap: Options A/B ignore the deductions for accumulated losses and deferred expenditure. Option C fabricates INR 100 crore (that's the SEBI-registered FPI Cat-I criteria, not AI). Always apply the exact net-worth formula specified in the framework. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C and XIX-A test body-corporate AI mechanics. XV Research Analyst and XXI-B Portfolio Manager also reference body-corporate AI. For Trusts (other than family trusts), the definition changes: NW = Book value of assets (excl intangibles) – book value of total liabilities — keep Trust vs body-corporate formulas separate. Manager's Pro-Tip: When onboarding corporate LPs, request the auditor's certificate specifying each line-item — don't rely on management-signed balance sheets. Deferred expenditure is a common sleeper: legal and pre-operative costs often sit there and swing NW below threshold.
